subproblem.title: A set agreeing near r₀u with a planar polar sector agrees with the plane near r₀u
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, all sets M, N ⊆ ℝ^P, orthonormal u, e ∈ ℝ^P and reals r₀, s with 0 < s < r₀ such that N is open, r₀u ∈ N and M ∩ N = {t(cos α·u + sin α·e) : t ∈ (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), α ∈ (−s, s)}: there is δ > 0 with M ∩ B_δ(r₀u) = span{u, e} ∩ B_δ(r₀u).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (M N : Set (Euclid P)) (u e : Euclid P) (r₀ s : ℝ), ‖u‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ u e = 0 → 0 < s → s < r₀ → IsOpen N → r₀ • u ∈ N → M ∩ N = (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • (Real.cos q.2 • u + Real.sin q.2 • e)) '' (Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ×ˢ Ioo (-s) s) → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ M ∩ ball (r₀ • u) δ = (Submodule.span ℝ {u, e} : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball (r₀ • u) δ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 12 (polar coordinates in Q and continuity of the angle at p). Notation: p := r₀u, Q := span{u, e}, B_r(x) := ball x r, f(y) := arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,u⟩). Note ⟨p,u⟩ = r₀, ⟨p,e⟩ = 0 and ‖p‖ = r₀.
1. (Choice of δ.) f is continuous at p, because y ↦ ⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,u⟩ is continuous wherever ⟨y,u⟩ ≠ 0 and ⟨p,u⟩ = r₀ > 0; and f(p) = arctan 0 = 0. Choose δ₁ > 0 with |f(y)| < s for y ∈ B_{δ₁}(p), and δ₂ > 0 with B_{δ₂}(p) ⊆ N (N is open and p ∈ N). Let δ := min(s, δ₁, δ₂) > 0.
2. (M ∩ B_δ(p) ⊆ Q.) If y ∈ M ∩ B_δ(p), then y ∈ M ∩ N (as B_δ(p) ⊆ N), so y = t(cos α·u + sin α·e) for some t, α; this is a linear combination of u and e, so y ∈ Q.
3. (Q ∩ B_δ(p) ⊆ M.) Let y ∈ Q ∩ B_δ(p). Write y = x·u + z·e (Submodule.mem_span_pair); by orthonormality ⟨y,u⟩ = x and ⟨y,e⟩ = z. Then x = ⟨p,u⟩ + ⟨y − p, u⟩ ≥ r₀ − ‖y − p‖ > r₀ − δ ≥ r₀ − s > 0. Let t := ‖y‖ = √(x² + z²) > 0 and α := arctan(z/x) = f(y). Then |t − r₀| = |‖y‖ − ‖p‖| ≤ ‖y − p‖ < δ ≤ s, so t ∈ (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), and |α| = |f(y)| < s, so α ∈ (−s, s). Moreover √(1 + (z/x)²) = t/x, so cos α = 1/√(1 + (z/x)²) = x/t and sin α = (z/x)/√(1 + (z/x)²) = z/t (Real.cos_arctan, Real.sin_arctan), whence t(cos α·u + sin α·e) = x·u + z·e = y. Hence y lies in the image set, which equals M ∩ N, so y ∈ M; and y ∈ B_δ(p).
4. (Conclusion.) By steps 2–3, M ∩ B_δ(r₀u) = span{u, e} ∩ B_δ(r₀u) with δ > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Pick δ ≤ s with B_δ(p) ⊆ N and |arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,u⟩)| < s on B_δ(p) (continuity of the angle at p = r₀u).
Points of M in B_δ(p) lie in M ∩ N, whose points are combinations of u and e, hence in span{u, e}.
A point y = x·u + z·e ∈ span{u, e} ∩ B_δ(p) has x > 0 and polar coordinates t = ‖y‖ ∈ (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), α = arctan(z/x) ∈ (−s, s), so y = t(cos α·u + sin α·e) ∈ M ∩ N.

audit.reason: All hypotheses match. The chosen δ ensures containment in N, positive first coordinate and both polar-coordinate bounds. The proof establishes both set inclusions and requires neither an unstated angular bound on s nor additional regularity of M.
